title: The Goalkeeper and the Chainsaw: from Palermo to the Casa Rosada
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Palermo, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested; full date given by both the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles. The hospital is not named in any source consulted, so the pin is the Palermo neighbourhood centroid, not a building.
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of October 1970 a son is born in Palermo to Norberto Horacio Milei, a bus driver who will come to own the company, and to Alicia Lujan Lucich. They name him Javier Gerardo. The family will move west to Villa Devoto and then to Saenz Pena, and the boy will grow up beside a sister, Karina, and under a father he later calls authoritarian. Palermo he returns to: fifty years on, in a park a short walk from this address, he launches the candidacy that carries him to the presidency of Argentina.
suggested_refs: The Palermo neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, birthplace and, in 2021, campaign-launch ground

stops.name: Colegio Cardenal Copello, the boy they call El Loco
stops.date_confidence: inferred; sources place the schooling in the 1980s at Villa Devoto without giving years. March 1983 is a placeholder for the start of an Argentine school year in that span.
stops.campa: The family lives in Villa Devoto and later in Saenz Pena, and the boy is sent to the Catholic Colegio Cardenal Copello. His classmates give him a name for the way he argues: El Loco, the madman, for outbursts that arrive at full volume and do not moderate. The name is not a schoolyard joke that fades. It follows him onto a football pitch, into lecture halls, into television studios, and at last onto ballot papers, where a country of forty-six million reads it as a description and not as an insult.
suggested_refs: Colegio Cardenal Copello, Villa Devoto, where the nickname El Loco is fixed
sources: Wikipedia (English), 'Javier Milei', on the move from Villa Devoto to Saenz Pena

stops.name: Estadio Chacarita Juniors, the goalkeeper
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span, dated to a single year by convention; the sources give a youth-division career of roughly 1983 to 1989 without naming seasons, so month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: Through the middle years of the 1980s he keeps goal in the youth divisions of Chacarita Juniors, at the ground in Villa Maipu. The goalkeeper is the one player set apart from his own side, alone in the position permitted to use its hands and blamed alone when the ball passes him. He plays there from about 1983 until the end of the decade. In 1989 Argentine prices rise by thousands of percent in a single year and the money in every pocket in the country dissolves. He is nineteen. He does not go back to football.
suggested_refs: Estadio Chacarita Juniors, Gutierrez 351, Villa Maipu, General San Martin

stops.name: Universidad de Belgrano, the average of 9.43
stops.date_confidence: contested; the Spanish Wikipedia biography puts the enrolment in 1988, while the geographic sourcing for the same article gives the study span as 1989-1993. Both are recorded; neither is adopted over the other. Month and day default to the March start of the Argentine academic year.
stops.campa: He enrols in economics at the Universidad de Belgrano and leaves it with an average of 9.43 out of ten, a mark that belongs to a quiet and orderly student rather than to the man shouting on television twenty-five years later. He begins two postgraduate degrees afterwards, one in economic theory at IDES and one at the Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, and finishes neither. The 9.43 stays on the record. So do the two unfinished programmes, and he lists all three for the rest of his career.
suggested_refs: Universidad de Belgrano, Zabala 1837, Buenos Aires
The unfinished postgraduate programmes at IDES and Universidad Torcuato Di Tella

stops.name: Banco Central, the internship on Reconquista
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Spanish Wikipedia gives the internship as December 1992 to June 1993. Coordinates corrected to Reconquista 266, the BCRA building itself, rather than the Plaza de Mayo pin the research pool had duplicated here.
stops.campa: From December 1992 to June 1993 he serves an internship at the Banco Central de la Republica Argentina, in the building on Reconquista in the financial district. He is twenty-two. The institution he is trained inside issues the currency and sets the price of credit, and it stands at the centre of every Argentine inflation of the century. Thirty years on he campaigns to close it. Six months is the entirety of his service to the Argentine state until the day, thirty-one years later, he is sworn in to run it.
suggested_refs: Banco Central de la Republica Argentina, Reconquista 266, Buenos Aires

stops.name: San Miguel de Tucuman, adviser to the province
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; month and day default to 01. The identity of the governor advised is contradicted between lenses of the research pool (Bussi in the chronology and in the Spanish Wikipedia text, Ramon Ortega in the geographic lens); the contradiction is recorded in the report and not resolved.
stops.campa: In 1994 he goes north to Tucuman as economic adviser to the provincial government of Antonio Domingo Bussi, the former army general who commanded the province under the dictatorship and now governs it by election. It is the only post of his working life held outside Buenos Aires, and the only one held inside a government until the presidency itself. He is twenty-three. He stays about a year, returns to the capital, and goes to work for a bank, and no Argentine government employs him again for twenty-nine years.
suggested_refs: Casa de Gobierno de Tucuman, San Miguel de Tucuman

stops.name: HSBC Buenos Aires, the peg breaks
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of appointment; month and day default to 01. The Spanish Wikipedia gives a tenure of roughly 1996 to 2002 without exact dates.
stops.campa: From 1996 he is senior economist at HSBC in Buenos Aires, and holds the post through the whole arc of the convertibility regime: the years when one peso is one dollar by law, the years when the law is believed, and the last months when it is not. In December 2001 the banks close their doors, deposits are frozen, and the presidency changes hands repeatedly inside a fortnight. He watches the peg break from inside a bank. He is thirty-one, and he keeps the post through the default and into the year the peso floats free.
suggested_refs: The 2001 corralito and the end of convertibility, watched from inside a commercial bank

stops.name: Maxima AFJP, the private pensions
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: In 2002, with the peg dead and the country in default, he becomes chief economist of Maxima AFJP, one of the private fund managers created to hold Argentine retirements outside the reach of the treasury. Six years after he leaves, the government of Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner nationalises the whole system and takes the funds back into public hands. He spends his early thirties learning the mechanics of the exact institution a later Peronist government abolishes.
suggested_refs: The AFJP private pension system, created 1994 and nationalised 2008

stops.name: Corporacion America, the house of Eurnekian
stops.date_confidence: contested; the Spanish Wikipedia dates the appointment to 2008, while the English article describes a tenure of about fifteen years as chief economist without naming a start year. 2008 is used as the earlier and more specific of the two, with the disagreement recorded.
stops.campa: He joins Corporacion America, the airport conglomerate of Eduardo Eurnekian, as chief economist and adviser on investment risk, and stays for roughly fifteen years. Eurnekian holds the concessions on most of the airports in Argentina; his economist is paid to say what the country will do next. Through these years Milei writes columns for La Nacion, El Cronista and Infobae, and begins to be asked onto television. The post runs some fifteen years, to the year he is elected president, and he is still drawing the salary while he campaigns against the caste.
suggested_refs: Corporacion America, the Eurnekian airport group, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Facultad de Ciencias Economicas, twenty years of lecturing
stops.date_confidence: attested from 2004 onward; month and day default to the March start of the academic year. The Spanish Wikipedia names him a professor of macroeconomics without giving an appointment date.
stops.campa: From 2004 he teaches macroeconomics at the Universidad de Buenos Aires and at other faculties in the city, standing in front of rooms of students for some twenty years. He teaches the standard curriculum: market structures, equilibrium, the theory of the firm, the conditions under which a market is said to fail. He is good at it and loud at it. The lecture hall is where the delivery is built, the pacing and the volume and the chalk. He will later say that everything he taught in that room about market structures was wrong, and that for twenty years he deceived the students in front of him.
suggested_refs: Facultad de Ciencias Economicas, Universidad de Buenos Aires, Av. Cordoba 2122

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the year he reads Rothbard
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; Stefanoni's article records the conversion and dates it to around 2013 without a month. Month and day default to 01. The lecture-hall pin is inherited from the teaching stop because the confession is about his own students.
stops.campa: Around 2013 he reads Murray Rothbard, and the reading undoes twenty years of his own teaching. The argument he finds there is that market failure is a category error, that what is called failure is an artefact of property rights left undefined, and that the state is not the corrective but the original offence. He is forty-two. The lineage he now claims runs back through Mises and Hayek to Adam Smith, whose invisible hand he will invoke on stages from Davos to Washington. He never teaches the old syllabus again.
stops.quote: Cuando termine de leer a Rothbard dije: 'Durante mas de 20 anos estuve enganando a mis alumnos. Todo lo que ensene sobre estructuras de mercado esta mal. Esta mal!'
stops.quote_source: Quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases: el paleolibertario que quiere tomar Argentina', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023. Diacritics stripped in this transcription; the source prints the accented Spanish.
suggested_refs: Murray Rothbard, Man, Economy, and State, the book named in the conversion account
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: America TV, Palermo, the studios
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the first television appearance (Hora Clave, 2015); month and day default to 01. The run on Animales Sueltos is dated in the sources only to 2015-2016.
stops.campa: He first appears as a television pundit on Hora Clave, and by 2015 he is a fixture in the studios of Palermo, most of all on Alejandro Fantino's Animales Sueltos. The format asks for an economist and gets a performer. He shouts. He calls the political class a caste, and he describes the state in images nobody else on Argentine television will say aloud. He has been writing sober newspaper columns since 2010 and almost nobody outside the profession reads them. Within three years he is the most interviewed economist in the country.
stops.quote: El Estado es el pedofilo en el jardin de infantes con los nenes encadenados y banados en vaselina.
stops.quote_source: Quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023; the article does not date the original occasion. Diacritics stripped in this transcription.
suggested_refs: Animales Sueltos, America TV, the programme that made him a national figure
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the five clones of Conan
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the dog's death and cloning and for the launch of the radio programme; neither is dated to a month in the sources, so month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: Conan, the English mastiff he took in around 2004 and called his four-legged son, dies. Milei sends genetic material to a company in the United States called PerPETuate and receives five puppies, and he names them for economists, Milton and Murray among them. The dead dog is thereby not dead, or is dead five times over, depending on who is asked. In the same year he begins hosting a weekly radio programme called Demoliendo Mitos, Demolishing Myths.
suggested_refs: PerPETuate Inc., the American cloning firm named in the Spanish Wikipedia account
sources: Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Javier Milei', personal life and media sections

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the consulting room on stage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the stage debut and of the media study; neither is dated to a month, so month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: He puts the act on a stage. El consultorio de Milei is a theatre show built out of the television persona, stand-up delivery wrapped around an economics lecture, and it sells. The same year a media study counts him the most interviewed economist on Argentine television: two hundred and thirty-five appearances, one hundred and ninety-three thousand three hundred and forty-seven seconds of airtime. That is fifty-three hours of one man talking about money on national television in a single year, three years before he holds any office.
suggested_refs: El consultorio de Milei, the 2018 stage show
The 2018 Argentine media study of economist airtime

segments.name: From the Screen to the Bench

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the party card
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Spanish Wikipedia. Pin corrected to the corpus city pin; the research pool had duplicated the Casa Rosada coordinates here for an event with no named venue.
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of February 2019 he formally joins the Partido Libertario. The step is a signature on the membership form of a party that has never elected anyone to anything. He is forty-eight. He has a theatre show, a radio programme, and the highest interview count of any economist in the country, and now he has a party card. Argentine politics at this moment is a closed contest between two coalitions, and neither of them notices. Within four years the card holder governs the country.
suggested_refs: Partido Libertario (Argentina), joined 23 February 2019

stops.name: Buenos Aires, on Viviana Canosa's programme
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; Stefanoni gives the programme and the year 2020 without a month or a broadcast date. Month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: On Viviana Canosa's programme he says the two sentences that will be played back at him for the rest of his life: that states are an invention of the Evil One, and that the pope is the representative of the Evil One on earth. The pope in question is Jorge Bergoglio, an Argentine, a porteno, born in a Buenos Aires neighbourhood not far from his own. Five years after this broadcast Milei will stand in Saint Peter's Square at that man's funeral, as head of the state that produced them both.
stops.quote: El papa es el representante del Maligno en la tierra.
stops.quote_source: Statement on Viviana Canosa's television programme, 2020, quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023
suggested_refs: Viviana Canosa's 2020 programme, source of both Maligno statements
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: Plaza Holanda, Palermo, the launch
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The research pool's causal ordering is corrected here: La Libertad Avanza was formed in July 2021, before this event, not shortly after it.
stops.campa: He launches his campaign for national deputy in Plaza Holanda, in Palermo, under a coalition banner assembled the month before and named La Libertad Avanza, Liberty Advances. He had announced the candidacy the previous September. The crowd in the park is young, mostly male, and larger than the party's own membership can explain, and it does not come from the neighbourhood committees and the unions that have supplied Argentine crowds for eighty years. It comes from the internet, and from the studios a few blocks from where he was born.
suggested_refs: Plaza Holanda, Parque Tres de Febrero, Palermo
sources: Wikipedia (English), 'Javier Milei', on the July 2021 formation of La Libertad Avanza

stops.name: Buenos Aires, three hundred and thirteen thousand votes
stops.date_confidence: attested; date corrected from the research pool, which gave 9 November. The 2021 Argentine general legislative election was held on 14 November and the primaries on 12 September, not in August as the pool stated.
stops.campa: In the September primaries the new coalition takes about fourteen percent of the vote in the City of Buenos Aires and becomes the third force in the capital overnight; the two editions of the encyclopaedia give the figure as 13.66 and 13.90. In the general election of the fourteenth of November it takes 313,808 votes, seventeen percent, and Javier Milei is elected national deputy. The coalitions that have divided Argentina between them for two decades read the result as a protest and expect it to pass.
suggested_refs: Argentine legislative elections of 2021, City of Buenos Aires returns

stops.name: Palacio del Congreso, sworn in as deputy
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both editions. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from the corpus pin for the Palacio del Congreso used in cristina_fernandez_de_kirchner.journey.json.
stops.campa: On the tenth of December 2021 he is sworn in as national deputy for the City of Buenos Aires, in the chamber under the bronze dome. The building is the one in which the laws of Juan Peron were passed and repealed and passed again, and it is the building whose occupants he has spent six years on television calling a caste. He announces that he will raffle his deputy's salary among the public every month. Two years to the day from this oath he takes another one in the same room, as president of the republic.
suggested_refs: Palacio del Congreso de la Nacion, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Catedra libre and General AnCap
stops.date_confidence: composite year-stop; the online programme is dated to 2022 without a month, the ESEADE honorary doctorate to December 2022, and the General AnCap utterance to 2022 at the Viva 22 event organised by Vox, whose location Stefanoni does not give. Month and day default to 01.
stops.campa: He keeps building the persona while holding the seat. He hosts an online programme called Catedra libre; the Instituto Universitario ESEADE gives him an honorary doctorate in December; and he appears in costume as General AnCap, an anarcho-capitalist superhero with a cape, a character made for conventions and then carried onto political stages abroad. He takes it onto a stage in Spain, at an event organised by the party Vox, and tells the audience his mission is to kick Keynesians and collectivists. He is a sitting member of the Argentine Chamber of Deputies while he says it.
stops.quote: Soy el general AnCap [anarcocapitalista]. Vengo de Liberland, una tierra creada por el principio de apropiacion originaria del hombre (...) Mi mision es cagar a patadas en el culo a keynesianos y colectivistas hijos de puta.
stops.quote_source: Quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023, which places the utterance at the Viva 22 event organised by the Spanish party Vox. Diacritics stripped in this transcription.
suggested_refs: The General AnCap costume persona
Instituto Universitario ESEADE, honorary doctorate, December 2022
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the presidential candidacy
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the English Wikipedia dates the official campaign launch to June 2022 without a day, and the research pool flags the month itself as reconstructed. Day defaults to 01.
stops.campa: In the middle of 2022 he announces that he will run for president of Argentina. He has been a deputy for six months and his party holds a handful of seats in a chamber of two hundred and fifty-seven. Inflation is running at a rate that will pass two hundred percent a year before the vote is taken. He campaigns with a chainsaw held over his head, promising to cut the state to the bone, to dollarise the currency, and to close the central bank he once interned in at twenty-two.
stops.quote: El primer gobierno de Menem fue el mejor de la historia argentina.
stops.quote_source: Campaign-era statement quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023
suggested_refs: The campaign chainsaw, carried through the 2023 Argentine presidential campaign
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the primary of August
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The vote share is given as 29.86 percent by the Spanish edition and as about 30 percent by the English; both are recorded and neither adopted over the other.
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of August 2023 he wins the open primary, the largest single share taken by any candidate, ahead of both coalitions that have governed Argentina since the return of democracy. The Spanish edition of the encyclopaedia gives the share as 29.86 percent, the English as about thirty. The peso falls the next morning. No poll had put him first. He has spent the campaign saying in public what no Argentine candidate says in public, and the vote grows as he goes on saying it.
stops.quote: Entre la mafia y el Estado prefiero a la mafia. La mafia tiene codigos, la mafia cumple, la mafia no miente, la mafia compite.
stops.quote_source: Interview given in Chile, quoted in Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023, in answer to a question about the Pinochet dictatorship. Diacritics stripped in this transcription.
suggested_refs: The 2023 Argentine presidential primaries (PASO), 13 August 2023
sources: Pablo Stefanoni, 'Javier Milei en 10 frases', Le Grand Continent, 18 September 2023

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the first round
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day.
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of October, his fifty-third birthday, the first round of the presidential election sends Sergio Massa and Javier Milei to a runoff. Massa is the sitting minister of economy of a government presiding over inflation of more than one hundred and forty percent a year, and he has just finished ahead of the man who promised to burn the apparatus down. Argentina is given a month to choose between the minister who ran the fire and the candidate who arrived with a chainsaw.
suggested_refs: Argentine general election, first round, 22 October 2023

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the runoff
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the vote total of 14,554,560 is from the Spanish edition. The campaign-headquarters pin is approximate: no source consulted names the venue from which he claimed victory.
stops.campa: On the nineteenth of November 2023 he takes 14,554,560 votes and the presidency of Argentina, by the widest margin of the democratic period. The Peronist movement, which has won most of the elections it has been permitted to contest since 1946, loses to a television economist with two years in the legislature and a party that did not exist three years ago. He is fifty-three. Three days later he tells an American interviewer what he intends to do, in the words he has been using since 2015.
stops.quote: The state does not create wealth; the state destroys it. The state can give you nothing because it produces nothing, and when it attempts it, it does so poorly.
stops.quote_source: The Rubin Report (BlazeTV), 22 November 2023, as compiled at en.wikiquote.org, 'Javier Milei'. The research pool attributed this to an interview with Tucker Carlson; the attribution is corrected here, and the wording is verified only against Wikiquote, a secondary compilation, since the primary outlet page returns HTTP 404.
suggested_refs: Argentine presidential runoff, 19 November 2023

stops.name: The Ohel, Old Montefiore Cemetery, Queens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Spanish Wikipedia article on his presidency.
stops.campa: Eight days after the election the president-elect flies to New York and goes to a cemetery in Queens, to the Ohel, the tomb of Menachem Mendel Schneerson, seventh rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, where the faithful come to leave written petitions at the grave. Milei is a baptised Catholic who studies Torah, keeps a rabbi at his side, and has spoken publicly of converting. He goes to the stone before he goes to the Casa Rosada. He is not yet sworn in; the inauguration is thirteen days away, in Buenos Aires.
suggested_refs: The Ohel at Old Montefiore Cemetery, Cambria Heights, Queens

stops.name: New York, lunch with Bill Clinton
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the English Wikipedia article on his presidency; the venue is not named in any source consulted, so the pin is the Manhattan centroid.
stops.campa: On the same New York visit he sits down to lunch with Bill Clinton and with the former senator Chris Dodd. Clinton was president of the United States through the years when the peso was pegged to the dollar and the Washington consensus was the whole of the argument in Latin America; Milei arrives promising to dollarise Argentina outright and abolish its central bank. Argentina is in default when the lunch is served. The president-elect is in New York for a single day, and he spends it at a grave and a lunch table.
suggested_refs: The 27 November 2023 New York meetings of the Argentine president-elect

stops.name: Palacio del Congreso, the oath
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The research pool located the swearing-in at the Casa Rosada; corrected here, the oath is taken before the Legislative Assembly at the Palacio del Congreso, with the handover of attributes following at the Casa Rosada.
stops.campa: On the tenth of December 2023 he takes the presidential oath before the Legislative Assembly in the Palacio del Congreso, in the same chamber where he swore in as a deputy exactly two years earlier. Then he walks out of the chamber and delivers his address on the steps outside, facing the crowd in the street rather than the deputies and senators behind him. There is no money, he tells them. The sentence he has repeated on television for eight years is now the stated fiscal policy of the Argentine Republic.
suggested_refs: Presidential inauguration of Javier Milei, Palacio del Congreso, 10 December 2023

stops.name: Casa Rosada, the sash and the guest from Kyiv
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the handover; the Zelenskyy visit is dated by the English article to December 2023 without a day and is placed here, at the inauguration he attended. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from the corpus Casa Rosada pin used across juan_peron.journey.json and cristina_fernandez_de_kirchner.journey.json.
stops.campa: He walks to the Casa Rosada and receives the sash and the baton in the room where they were handed to Juan Peron in 1946, to Isabel Peron in 1974, and to Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner in 2007. She is the outgoing vice president; she leaves the building on the day he enters it. Among the foreign guests is Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has flown out of a country at war to meet a president whose predecessors kept Argentina carefully neutral. The shock therapy is announced within hours: the peso devalued by more than half, subsidies cut.
suggested_refs: Casa Rosada, Balcarce 50, Buenos Aires, the handover of presidential attributes

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Decree 70 of 2023
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; the English article dates the decree and the rent-control repeal to December 2023 without days. The twentieth is used as the decree's number-bearing date and should be verified against the Boletin Oficial before this stop is treated as day-precise.
stops.campa: Days into the presidency he signs Decree 70 of 2023, a decree of necessity and urgency that repeals or amends hundreds of laws at once: rent control gone, export rules gone, labour law rewritten, whole registers of state regulation struck out in a single instrument by a president whose party holds a fraction of both chambers. Argentina keeps a constitutional device for governing without the legislature, and he reaches for it in his second week. The labour confederations call a general strike for January.
stops.quote: If printing money could end poverty, printing diplomas could end stupidity.
stops.quote_source: Quoted with attribution to Milei in 'Don't cry for Milei, Argentina', The Spectator Australia, December 2023; wording confirmed against the published article
suggested_refs: Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia 70/2023, Boletin Oficial de la Republica Argentina
sources: The Spectator Australia, 'Don't cry for Milei, Argentina', December 2023

stops.name: Davos, the Congress Centre
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the transcript was read through a secondary mirror of the Eurasia Review text rather than the original outlet page.
stops.campa: Six weeks into the presidency he stands in the Congress Centre at Davos and tells the assembled owners of the world that the West is in danger and that they are the danger. Socialism is impoverishing and murderous, he says; there is no such thing as market failure; do not be intimidated by the political caste. The audience is the World Economic Forum, an institution his own supporters treat as the headquarters of everything he opposes, and it applauds him. The speech leaves the hall and runs for months on the internet.
stops.quote: Today I'm here to tell you that the Western world is in danger. And it is in danger because those who are supposed to have to defend the values of the West are co-opted by a vision of the world that inexorably leads to socialism and thereby to poverty.
stops.quote_source: Speech to the World Economic Forum, Davos, 18 January 2024; transcript as published by Eurasia Review, read via a secondary mirror rather than the original page
suggested_refs: The Davos Congress Centre address of 18 January 2024
sources: Eurasia Review transcript of the Davos address, via mirror

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the general strike
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by the English article, which dates the strike against Decree 70/2023 to January 2024 without a day; the twenty-fourth is the date reported in contemporary coverage and should be checked before being treated as day-precise here.
stops.campa: He comes home from the Alps to a country shut down against him. The labour confederation calls the general strike, the same apparatus that Juan Peron built into the spine of Argentine politics and that Eva Peron addressed from balconies. It is the earliest general strike called against any Argentine government since the return of democracy. Inflation for the twelve months to December 2023 stands at two hundred and eleven percent; it will climb to two hundred and eighty-nine percent by April before it turns.
suggested_refs: The January 2024 Argentine general strike against Decree 70/2023
sources: Wikipedia (English), 'Presidency of Javier Milei', inflation figures

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Western Wall
stops.date_confidence: contested; the geographic lens of the research pool dates the visit to February 2024 with rabbi Axel Wahnish, while the interlock lens calls it a 2023 pilgrimage. February 2024 is adopted as the better-sourced of the two and the disagreement is recorded. Day is not given in any source consulted. Coordinates inherited byte-identical from the corpus Temple Mount pin used in abraham.journey.json.
stops.campa: He goes to Jerusalem with his rabbi, Axel Wahnish, and prays at the Western Wall, the retaining wall of the second temple platform, where petitions are folded into the joints of the stone. He weeps at the wall in front of the cameras. He states that Argentina will move its embassy to Jerusalem. A baptised Catholic president of the country with the largest Jewish population in Latin America, a country that took in both the refugees of Europe and the men who had hunted them, stands with his forehead against the Kotel.

stops.name: National Harbor, the American right adopts him
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Washington trip of 23-24 February 2024 is listed in the English Wikipedia article on his international trips. The research pool placed the chainsaw handover at this appearance; that is corrected, the chainsaw belongs to the February 2025 visit.
stops.campa: He flies from Jerusalem to Washington and speaks at the Conservative Political Action Conference at the Gaylord National Resort, National Harbor, where he meets Donald Trump, then a candidate under indictment and not yet president a second time. He addresses the conference as a sitting head of state, and the room takes him for one of its own. In April his government files to become a global partner of NATO, an application from a country that spent forty years defining itself against exactly that alignment.

stops.name: Palacio del Congreso, the Ley de Bases
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; date corrected from the research pool, which gave July 2024. Congress gave final approval on 27 June 2024, and July is the month of promulgation.
stops.campa: On the twenty-seventh of June 2024 Congress gives final approval to the Ley de Bases, the omnibus reform the government has spent six months cutting down to something that will pass: delegated powers, privatisations, a tax amnesty, an incentive regime for very large investments. Outside the building the police clear the street with gas while the vote is taken inside. It is the first statute of his presidency, and he has governed for two hundred days without one.

stops.name: New York, the General Assembly
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; contemporary coverage places the address in the September 2024 general debate without a day being given in the sources consulted. The twenty-fourth is the conventional opening week and should be verified.
stops.campa: In September he addresses the General Assembly of the United Nations and tells it that the organisation is a bureaucracy of the ideology of death: redistribution, abortion rights, the agenda for 2030. Argentina begins voting alone, or almost alone, on resolution after resolution in that chamber. The country that gave the world Raul Prebisch and the doctrine of the periphery now votes against the coordinating machinery it once argued for, and the delegate saying so is its president.

stops.campa: He crosses the river to Montevideo for the sixty-fifth Mercosur summit and stands beside Ursula von der Leyen as the European Union and Mercosur announce, after twenty-five years of negotiation, that they have an agreement. Milei takes the rotating presidency of the bloc in the same week. He has spent a career calling Mercosur a customs cartel, and he now chairs it, and the deal he inherits is the largest opening of the Argentine economy since the convertibility years he watched break from inside a bank.

The instrument Milei carried through an Argentine campaign as a promise to cut the state has become the emblem of an American department founded to do the same thing. He raised it first over a crowd in Buenos Aires, and he gives it away on a stage in Maryland.

stops.name: Casa Rosada, two judges by decree
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the English Wikipedia article.
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of February 2025 he appoints Manuel Garcia-Mansilla and Ariel Lijo to the Supreme Court of Argentina by presidential decree, bypassing the Senate confirmation the constitution requires. Garcia-Mansilla is sworn in and takes his seat. The clause invoked was written for a republic whose Congress met for half of the year and could not be assembled in time; it is used here in an age of aeroplanes, against a chamber sitting three blocks from the president's desk.

stops.name: Palacio del Congreso, the Senate refuses
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the English Wikipedia article.
stops.campa: On the fourth of April the Senate rejects both nominations outright, and the judge who had been seated by decree leaves the court he had been sitting on for five weeks. It is the first defeat of the presidency that cannot be undone by issuing another decree. The chamber he has called a caste of parasites uses the one power he has no instrument against. It votes no, in session and on the record, in the building where he swore both of his oaths, and the refusal stands.

stops.name: Saint Peter's Square, the funeral of Francis
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; sourced to contemporary international coverage rather than to an encyclopaedia article.
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of April 2025 he stands in Saint Peter's Square at the funeral of Pope Francis. Five years before, on Argentine television, he called this man the representative of the Evil One on earth. Since taking office he has met him and embraced him and said nothing further of the kind. Jorge Bergoglio, born in Buenos Aires in 1936, never once returned to Argentina as pope, and the head of state of the country they were both born in stands in the square, among the sovereigns, to watch him buried.

stops.campa: On the seventh of September 2025 La Libertad Avanza loses the Buenos Aires provincial election, and loses it heavily, in the province that holds four in every ten Argentine voters. stops.name: Buenos Aires, the midterm landslide

stops.campa: Seven weeks after losing the province he wins the midterm legislative elections in a landslide. The party that held two deputies in 2021 now commands the largest bloc in the chamber where he swore his first oath. The Peronist movement of Juan Peron, of Eva Peron, of Isabel Peron and of Jose Lopez Rega, which has organised Argentine politics for eighty years, has been beaten in a national election by a man who was still a television pundit when its last president took office.
